skill.description: Generate Kling 3.0 videos on RunComfy through Standard, Pro, and 4K endpoints for text-to-video and image-to-video workflows.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backticks, documentation URLs, placeholder HTTPS examples, or documented CLI token storage. No prompt injection attempt or malicious exfiltration instruction was found. One semantic issue remains because inline shell JSON examples can be unsafe with raw user prompts.

remediation.issue: Inline JSON is shown inside single-quoted shell commands.
remediation.suggestion: Show a safer invocation that writes the request body to a JSON file or uses an argument array. Remove the blanket no shell-injection claim.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Shell Quoting Guidance for Prompt Input
semantic_findings.description: The examples pass user-controlled prompt JSON through a single-quoted shell argument while claiming there is no shell-injection surface. An agent could insert raw prompt text containing quotes and change the shell command.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill shows inline Bash JSON examples and separately states that CLI input has no shell-injection surface. The risk depends on how an agent interpolates user prompts, so confidence is high enough to remediate but not certain.

content.value_statement: Creating cinematic video variants across tiers can be slow and error-prone. This skill routes Kling 3.0 text or image prompts to the right RunComfy endpoint.
actual_capabilities: Selects Standard, Pro, or 4K Kling 3.0 tiers based on quality and budget needs.
Supports text-to-video and image-to-video requests across six RunComfy endpoints.
Builds prompts with duration, aspect ratio, audio, seed, and negative prompt options.
Uses source and tail image URLs for image-to-video start and end frame control.
Explains RunComfy CLI setup, login, exit codes, output downloads, and cost tradeoffs.
limitations: Requires RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, a token, and network access.
Image-to-video requires publicly fetchable HTTPS image URLs. Local files are not supported.
Each generation is limited to 15 seconds and fixed supported aspect ratios.
4K and audio options can increase cost, bandwidth use, and output file size.

use_cases.title: Prototype Social Video Variants
use_cases.description: Create quick 9:16 or 1:1 draft clips for social campaigns before buying higher quality renders.

use_cases.title: Produce Brand Film Shots
use_cases.description: Route polished storyboards to Pro or 4K endpoints for cinematic ad clips with stable characters.

use_cases.title: Animate Reference Images
use_cases.description: Turn product photos, portraits, or concept frames into motion while preserving the source subject.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Quick Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a 5 second Kling 3.0 Standard text-to-video clip. Scene: [scene]. Aspect ratio: [ratio]. No audio.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Source Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate this HTTPS image with Kling 3.0 image-to-video. Preserve the subject, add [motion], and keep the clip under [duration] seconds.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multi-Shot Ad
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Kling V3.0 Pro for a multi-shot ad. Include three shots, synchronized ambience, and a negative prompt for unwanted artifacts.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a 4K Master
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Kling V3.0 4K plan with tier choice, prompt segments, audio guidance, seed strategy, expected cost, and output settings.

output_examples.input: Create a fast vertical coffee shop clip for a social post.
output_examples.output: Recommended Standard text-to-video, 5 seconds, 9:16, no audio. The prompt emphasizes handheld close-up motion, steam, and warm cafe ambience.

output_examples.input: Animate a product photo for a premium landing page.
output_examples.output: Recommended Pro image-to-video using the product image URL. The plan preserves the product shape while adding slow camera movement and soft lighting.

output_examples.input: Make a finished 4K brand film shot with sound.
output_examples.output: Recommended 4K text-to-video with audio enabled. The response includes a concise shot sequence, cost warning, and output directory guidance.

best_practices: Start with Standard tier to test motion, framing, duration, and prompt language.
Use image-to-video when exact product identity, face identity, or composition must stay stable.
Keep prompts specific about camera motion, shot order, lighting, audio, and negative constraints.
anti_patterns: Do not use 4K for early experiments when Standard can validate the concept.
Do not request unsupported aspect ratios or clips longer than 15 seconds.
Do not pass private image URLs unless they are approved for RunComfy processing.

faq.question: Does this skill require a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need the RunComfy CLI, login, and a valid token before generation works.

faq.question: Which Kling 3.0 tiers are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Standard, Pro, and 4K tiers for text-to-video and image-to-video.

faq.question: Can it animate a local image file?
faq.answer: No. Image-to-video requires a publicly fetchable HTTPS image URL.

faq.question: Can Kling 3.0 generate audio?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports the audio option and explains when it changes cost.

faq.question: What is the maximum clip duration?
faq.answer: Each Kling 3.0 generation can be up to 15 seconds.

faq.question: Does it choose between text-to-video and image-to-video?
faq.answer: Yes. It selects the mode from whether you provide a source image.
